physical_mismatches.reason: The paper gives no per-block floorplan (x, y, width, height) and no per-block watts for the 256-core SCC chip. Only a hot spot power density of 216.6 W/cm2 is stated, so no complete experiment can be reconstructed. The power profile comes from prior work (Eris et al.), which is not packaged.

The scenario reports simulation speed (Table IV). Its temperature results are not available in the extractable text, so no paper thermal observable value exists for comparison. The ~90 degC maximum and ~9 degC gradient quoted on page 11 belong to the separate OpenROAD MPSoC scenario.

The original solver is a compact RC netlist solved by Xyce on an MPI cluster, with a medium-cost heat spreader and heat sink, and the grid resolution is given only in Table III. A Studio solver, package and cooling model will differ in discretization and boundary conditions, so temperatures are not directly comparable.
The scenario has no optimizer and no controller, and the power trace is a single selected profile. The original does not exercise any optimizer or controller behavior to replicate.

The paper's monolithic 3-D, liquid-microchannel and 2.5-D PNoC cases are separate scenarios and are not used. The selected case is 2-D with a conventional heat sink, so no 3-D or interposer mismatch applies to the selected scenario.

studio_assumptions: No Studio package or material assumptions are supplied in the packet, so none can be recorded as paper-derived. Any Studio default stack, materials and heat sink would differ from the paper's medium-cost heat sink.
Any placement the runner generates would be illustrative and separate from paper facts, and its temperatures must not be numerically compared to the paper.
